ChipsSelection

The `m3e-chip` component — strict per-component surface.

import M3e
import M3e.Values
These helpers are our examples, not the library

The Doc.* helpers in these examples are this docs app's own module — not part of elm-m3e (they won't resolve from a fresh install). You rarely need anything like them. The library gives you typed components (M3e.*) plus TypedHtml for standard HTML, and you never import HtmlIr: M3e.Element, M3e.Attr, M3e.Node, M3e.Values.Value and M3e.Kind.Supported / .Shared are all re-exported, so every type annotation you need is reachable from the brand. Build layout, text, and links directly from those. The genuine escapes ship with the library too, in one greppable, lint-fenced place — M3e.Unsafe (fromHtml, fromNode, recast, and customElement for a custom tag the types can't express) and M3e.Unsafe.Attributes. See Escapes.

Usage

Non-interactive chips

M3ecomponentbuildHTML
M3e.chipSet []
…
[ M3e.chip [] [ Kit.text "Confidential" ]
, M3e.chip [] [ Kit.text "Draft" ]
, M3e.chip [] [ Kit.text "Finance" ]
, M3e.chip [] [ Kit.text "Presentation" ]
]
M3e.ChipSet.view []
…
[ M3e.Chip.el { content = Kit.text "Confidential" } [] []
, M3e.Chip.el { content = Kit.text "Draft" } [] []
, M3e.Chip.el { content = Kit.text "Finance" } [] []
, M3e.Chip.el { content = Kit.text "Presentation" } [] []
]
M3e.ChipSet.build
|> M3e.ChipSet.withChild (M3e.Chip.view [] [ Kit.text "Confidential" ])
|> M3e.ChipSet.withChild (M3e.Chip.view [] [ Kit.text "Draft" ])
|> M3e.ChipSet.withChild (M3e.Chip.view [] [ Kit.text "Finance" ])
|> M3e.ChipSet.withChild (M3e.Chip.view [] [ Kit.text "Presentation" ])
|> M3e.ChipSet.toElement
<m3e-chip-set>
…
<m3e-chip>Confidential</m3e-chip>
<m3e-chip>Draft</m3e-chip>
<m3e-chip>Finance</m3e-chip>
<m3e-chip>Presentation</m3e-chip>
</m3e-chip-set>

Variants

M3ecomponentbuildHTML
[ M3e.chip [] [ Kit.text "Outlined" ]
, M3e.chip [ M3e.Chip.variant M3e.Values.elevated ] [ Kit.text "Elevated" ]
]
[ M3e.Chip.el { content = Kit.text "Outlined" } [] []
, M3e.Chip.el { content = Kit.text "Elevated" } [ M3e.Chip.variant M3e.Values.elevated ] []
]
[ M3e.Chip.build { content = Kit.text "Outlined" }
|> M3e.Chip.toElement
, M3e.Chip.build { content = Kit.text "Elevated" }
|> M3e.Chip.withVariant M3e.Values.elevated
|> M3e.Chip.toElement
]
<m3e-chip>Outlined</m3e-chip>
<m3e-chip variant="elevated">Elevated</m3e-chip>

|> M3e.Chip.toElement

Disabling

M3ecomponentbuildHTML
[ M3e.assistChip [ M3e.AssistChip.disabled True ] [ Kit.text "Disabled" ]

[ M3e.AssistChip.build { content = Kit.text "Disabled" }
|> M3e.AssistChip.withDisabled True
|> M3e.AssistChip.toElement

|> M3e.AssistChip.withDisabledInteractive True
|> M3e.AssistChip.toElement
]

<m3e-assist-chip disabled-interactive="">Disabled Interactive</m3e-assist-chip>

API

Types

type Is

The kind row m3e-chip produces (open — composes into any slot naming it).

type Attrs

The closed attribute-capability row.

type Builder

The narrowed pipe-builder this component's M3e.Build.<X> module exposes.

type AttrCaps

The attribute capabilities this component's builder admits.

type SlotCaps

The singular-slot capabilities this component's builder admits.

type Content

The kinds the default slot admits.

type IconSlot

The kinds the icon slot admits.

type TrailingIconSlot

The kinds the trailing-icon slot admits.

type ChildAdmittedBy

The context demand this container injects into each child's admittedBy row.

type Variant

The variant values valid on this component (compile-tight narrowing).

M3eComponentsBuilderRaw

Constructor

chip : List.List (M3e.Attr M3e.Component.Chip.Attrs msg) -> List.List (M3e.Element M3e.Component.Chip.Content (M3e.Component.Chip.ChildAdmittedBy childAdm) msg) -> M3e.Element (M3e.Component.Chip.Is s) admittedBy msg

The loose m3e-chip producer — open attribute/child rows, no required record. See M3e.Component.Chip.component for the required-content form.

Advanced

Motion durations and state-layer opacities — raw CSS custom-property overrides for the 16 transition-timing tokens and 3 interaction-state opacity tokens @m3e/web exposes.

CSS Variables

Non-color @m3e/web CSS custom properties (typescale, shape, motion, state), grouped by name hierarchy. Color tokens live in the Color section. Type a value to override it; clear it to revert. Live default values are not shown — Elm cannot read computed CSS variables.
